corrections.originalCritique: Strongest feature: The response exposes an authentic weakness in crude preference satisfaction by showing that variable desires alone cannot determine moral status without attention to consent, coercion, agency, and the character of the act. Principal limitation: It attributes that crude theory to a broader secular position that had already invoked potential conscious states, impartial rules, and social consequences, so its generalized conclusion misses decisive components of the immediate proposal. Live burden: The objection must address the strongest welfare-and-rule account and demonstrate that recipient variation defeats its impartial criteria rather than merely producing different outcomes under relevantly different conditions. Locked score: The supplied weak band reflects a clear and locally relevant example whose overextended scope, reduced representation of the opposing view, and limited responsiveness prevent it from establishing the absence of secular objectivity.

lockedMove.speaker: Matt Slick
lockedMove.proposition: A recipient-preference account can assign opposite moral statuses to the same conduct depending on what a recipient wants and therefore cannot furnish an objective standard.
